_comment: The provider ROLE catalog. HG-0008 says the harness names roles, never vendors — but until now the only place a vendor could be named was adapters/reference/, which holds at most ONE adapter per control (AD-R05 refuses two on the same control, and CI mounts that whole directory). So a role with three plausible providers had nowhere to put the second and third: the directory encoded 'the one true instance', not 'pick one'. This catalog is the fix. Each role states the control it fills and the capability name a profile uses to REQUIRE it; providers/<role>/ holds the alternatives; docs/governance/provider-selection.json records which one this institution chose. Nothing here is mounted by default — a catalog is an offer, not an installation.

roles.purpose: Assert the dependency-audit severity counts from outside the repository under test, so the Q4 gate cannot be satisfied by an agent writing its own verdict
must_provide: severity counts (and any reachability verdict) asserted by the scanning platform, not by the scanned repo
a tamper probe: editing the local report away from the platform's counts must fail the build

roles.purpose: Make the runtime the coding agent executes in a digest-pinned, attestation-verified image, so HG-0011's attested-execution limb rests on evidence rather than on a base image nobody can account for
must_provide: a digest (never a tag) plus a verification result for the image's SBOM and provenance
a negative probe: an image without a valid attestation must fail admission

roles.purpose: Record which system of record carries the institution's ISSC arrangement — membership, HSA approvals, resolutions and minutes — so an Islamic product plan cannot compile against a Shari'ah governance function that exists only as prose
must_provide: the ISSC register exported to docs/governance/issc-register.json — seats with their HSA approval and appointment references, and the resolutions an approval cites — asserted by the system of record, not by the repository under test
a tamper probe: a register row that diverges from the system of record (a seat added, an approval reference edited) must fail reconciliation
roles._comment: DORMANT UNLESS AN ISLAMIC PRODUCT IS IN FLIGHT. `shariah_governance` compiles only from an Islamic product or institution profile, so a conventional adopter never meets this role — PS-R06 arms it the moment a plan names the capability and not before. And note what the role does NOT do: it fixes WHERE the committee's arrangement is recorded and proves the export matches. Scholars decide Shari'ah. No provider here, and no gate that reads its evidence, rules on any Shari'ah question — they check that a ruling exists, is attributable to an approved committee, and is bound to this change.

roles.purpose: Name the policy-enforcement point that constrains agents in the SERVING path (input/output filters, tool-use allowlists, terminology and PII screens) so the runtime guardrail is a chosen, evidenced component rather than an assumption
must_provide: an enforcement decision log asserted by the serving platform — the enforcement point itself — and never by the agent being constrained
a negative probe: a policy-violating action must be denied and the denial must be observable in that log
roles._comment: Do not confuse this with guardrails/guardrail-policy.json: that policy covers the agent that WRITES the code, at build time; this role covers the agent that SERVES the customer, at request time. The honest limit is the same in both places — the harness reads records, it does not watch production. It cannot verify that a runtime guardrail FIRES; it can refuse to let a change ship that never chose one, and it can read the denial the platform recorded when the negative probe was run.

roles.purpose: Name the platform controls that stand between real customer data and the people and agents who touch it — key custody and rotation, field-level encryption or tokenisation, and access logging — so an institution moving off synthetic data records what it CHOSE instead of inheriting the harness's synthetic-only posture by silence
must_provide: key custody and access logs asserted by the PLATFORM that holds the data — the key manager, the tokenisation service, the database audit log — and never by the application or the agent that reads through them
a negative probe: an unauthorised read must be DENIED and the denial must be observable in that log. An allow-only log proves traffic, never protection
roles._comment: THE SEAM THIS ROLE EXISTS TO MAKE VISIBLE. Everything else in this bundle assumes synthetic data — pii-guard.sh blocks real-PII shapes at the keystroke, and REAL-PII-SURFACE is graded `absent` in the control catalog because the harness genuinely ships nothing for the real-data case. That is honest while the repository is synthetic-only. The moment an institution points a workload at production data, the same `absent` grade reads as 'not our problem' about the surface that now matters most, and nothing in the tree changes to say so. This role turns that transition into a recorded choice: an adopter that moves to real data must name the key manager, the encryption or tokenisation boundary, and the access log, and evidence a denial. What the role does NOT do: it does not encrypt anything, does not verify a key rotation happened, and cannot see a read at request time. The harness reads JSON records; it never watches production. It refuses to let the move to real data happen without a named, evidenced control, which is a smaller claim than 'customer data is protected' and is the true one.
roles._dormancy_comment: DORMANT UNLESS A COMPILED PLAN REQUIRES IT. `real_data_controls` arms via PS-R06 only when a profile a change compiles against demands it — the intended home is a regulated-institution profile at the high tier, where real customer data is in scope. A repository working on synthetic fixtures never meets this role.
